whatThePageStates: The page is a single five-column table (Region name, Region, Control plane endpoint, Protocol, Support date) listing the AWS Regions in which AWS CloudTrail is available, with 36 data rows. Presence in the table is the whole coverage claim: each row names a Region, its control plane endpoint hostname, the protocol (HTTPS for every row), and the date CloudTrail became available there. The page states no negatives — there is no No column, no exclusion list, and no statement that any Region lacks CloudTrail. A leading note redirects readers elsewhere for CloudTrail Lake Regions and for data plane endpoints, and two trailing notes point at GovCloud and China endpoint references; none of those carry coverage values for this page.

features.statuses: 36 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 36+0+0=36. This is a presence-only (listed = supported) table: every one of the 36 data rows is an affirmative availability statement. The Protocol column is HTTPS on all 36 rows and the Support date column is populated on all 36 rows, so neither column encodes a status distinction. Not-supported is ABSENT, never stated — the page never names a Region where CloudTrail is unavailable, so no No count may be derived by subtracting from any external Region total.
features.scope: None. There is no second dimension. The table has one row per Region and no per-plan, per-scan-method or per-feature sub-dimension. The endpoint hostname, protocol and support date are attributes of the same single claim, not scopes that split it. CloudTrail Lake Region support is explicitly a different page and must not be treated as a second scope here.
features.reasoning: The enumerated thing is the AWS Region, a universe that exists independently of CloudTrail, so the axis is region and the kind is external. The unit of claim is one Region — the Region column holds 36 unique codes (us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2, af-south-1, ap-east-1, ap-south-1, ap-south-2, ap-northeast-1, ap-northeast-2, ap-northeast-3, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-southeast-3, ap-southeast-4, ap-southeast-5, ap-southeast-7, ca-central-1, ca-west-1, cn-north-1, cn-northwest-1, eu-central-1, eu-central-2, eu-north-1, eu-south-1, eu-south-2, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-west-3, il-central-1, mx-central-1, me-central-1, me-south-1, sa-east-1, us-gov-east-1, us-gov-west-1) against 36 rows, so rows and axis values are one-to-one and there is no collapse.

shouldNotExtract: The table header row and the markdown separator row are not data. The Protocol column (HTTPS, identical on every row) is a transport fact, not a coverage status. The Support date column is a launch date, not a status value. The leading Note block is cross-page navigation: the CloudTrail Lake supported Regions link and the AWS General Reference data plane endpoints link are pointers to other pages and carry no counts here. The two trailing paragraphs linking to the AWS GovCloud (US) Service Endpoints page and the Endpoints and ARNs for AWS in China page are references, not coverage rows. The whole See also section — the optional Skills for AI coding assistants boilerplate and its aws agent-toolkit search-skills command — is generic AWS-wide footer text and must never be harvested. The anchor tags (<a name=...>) are markup.
coverageDimensions: REGION: fully given — 36 named Regions, each an affirmative availability statement, spanning the commercial partition plus 2 China Regions (cn-north-1, cn-northwest-1) and 2 GovCloud Regions (us-gov-east-1, us-gov-west-1). SERVICE: gives nothing. The page is about exactly one service, AWS CloudTrail, and enumerates no other services; any per-service coverage figure taken from this page is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE: gives nothing. No resource types, event sources, trail types or data event categories are enumerated anywhere on the page; any resource-type figure attributed to this page is fabricated. The page is likewise silent on partitions as an axis — the partition is inferable from the Region codes but is never enumerated or counted as its own list.
trap: The single most likely misparse is inventing a No side: treating this presence-only list as a Yes/No matrix and subtracting 36 from some external count of all AWS Regions to manufacture unsupported Regions. The page never states a negative, so the only defensible split is 36 Yes and 0 No. Runners-up: (1) reading the Protocol column as a status and scoring 36 HTTPS values as a second feature, or reading the Support date column as a tri-state; (2) counting 38 pipe-prefixed lines, or 37, by including the header and/or separator row instead of the 36 data rows; (3) following the leading note and folding CloudTrail Lake Region support into this page's count, when CloudTrail Lake is a separate page with its own, different Region list; (4) harvesting the See also Skills for AI coding assistants bullet or the GovCloud and China reference paragraphs as coverage items; (5) treating the endpoint hostnames as a distinct axis, which would double-count the same 36 claims.
